knownIssuesApplied.note: reflax-yield-vault has knownIssuesCount=0 and knownIssues=[] in registered-projects.json. No project-level known-issue suppressions were applied. The designDecisions array documents acknowledged protocol behaviours (principal decremented by requested amount, bidirectional routes, slippage in bps, two-phase withdrawal) but these are intent records, not suppressible known issues, unless a deduped finding's ENTIRE claim is covered by a design-decision entry.

removals.matchedTo: L-02: skimSurplus unbounded iteration over owner-grown authorized-client set (no pagination)
removals.matchBasis: Exact semantic match. DEDUP-013 (_accrueSurplusShares / _distributeBuffer unbounded iteration OOG) and L-02 (skimSurplus unbounded loop over authorized-client EnumerableSet) describe the same root cause: the owner-managed client set has no on-chain cap, so a sufficiently large set causes OOG on every skimSurplus call. L-02's wont-fix triage note ('likely no more than 3 clients') remains authoritative. story-042 doubled the per-iteration constant (parallel _distributeBuffer pass) but L-02 was already reconfirmed wont-fix with that fact noted. DEDUP-013 adds no new attack vector beyond what L-02 already documents.

removals.matchedTo: NatSpec on _accrueSurplusShares / setSetAsideBuffer explicitly acknowledges deposit-dilution as an accepted tradeoff
removals.matchBasis: DEDUP-018 (multi-client deposit dilution: late depositors erode early depositors' accrued surplus via proportional allocation) is self-described by the deduplicator as 'documented design behaviour'. The finding's own rootCause text states: 'The setSetAsideBuffer NatSpec explicitly acknowledges this as a known acceptable tradeoff for the current all-protocol-owned-client model.' The buffer front-run sub-case (ECON-010) is likewise noted as acknowledged in NatSpec. A finding whose entire impact is covered by acknowledged NatSpec design documentation is treated equivalently to a known issue. This is also consistent with the designDecisions entry for reflax-yield-vault in registered-projects.json: 'Principal is decremented by REQUESTED amount on withdraw, not RECEIVED amount (any shortfall accrues to protocol)' — establishing that slippage/rounding residuals are deliberately protocol-owned surplus, the same philosophy behind deposit dilution.

removals.matchedTo: Pure QA gas inefficiency — no security impact; equivalent to unused-view-function category
removals.matchBasis: DEDUP-020 reports that AYieldStrategy._initiateWithdrawal calls this.balanceOf() as an external call rather than an internal virtual dispatch, paying the external-call gas premium unnecessarily. The finding itself classifies the impact as 'Gas inefficiency only. No security impact.' and its estimatedSeverity is 'informational'. Per CLAUDE.md: 'Unused view functions (QA at best)' is a known invalid pattern; pure gas inefficiency findings with zero security impact fall into the same category. No PoC path to fund loss or protocol function impairment exists.

removals.matchedTo: Code-quality-only finding — Solidity 0.8+ default-initializes uint256 to 0; no security impact
removals.matchBasis: DEDUP-022 reports that the local variable totalSetAside in _distributeBuffer is declared but not explicitly initialized. The finding itself states: 'No security impact in Solidity 0.8+ (default initialization to 0). Code quality finding only.' The accumulator behaves correctly because Solidity guarantees uint256 zeroing. There is no attack path. Per C4 norms and CLAUDE.md standards: common automated-tool findings without a demonstrated HM exploit path are known-invalid patterns. This is a Slither low-quality report (SLITHE-005) on an unchanged contract pattern.

stillOpenMatches.matchBasis: DEDUP-004 (slippageToleranceBps defaults to 0 at deployment and accepts MAX_BPS) and L-01 (slippageToleranceBps default-0 plus setter missing sane cap) share the same contract (ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol), the same setter function (setSlippageTolerance), and the same state variable (slippageToleranceBps). L-01 is open and explicitly covers the zero-default and missing-cap sub-issues. The run-08 note on L-01 already expanded its blast radius to cover the deposit-side haircut.
stillOpenMatches.newEvidenceNote: DEDUP-004 contributes two sub-cases NOT previously documented in L-01: (1) MAX_BPS (10000) is an explicitly valid setSlippageTolerance input, and at MAX_BPS the formula amount*(10000-10000)/10000 = 0 silently nullifies ALL depositor principal — not just reduces it, but fully discards it while consuming tokens. (2) Halmos (SYMBOLIC-001) formally proves a dust-loss edge case at any non-trivial slippage setting: deposits smaller than 10000/(10000-slippageBps) also receive zero credited principal. These two attack surfaces are substantively more severe than the existing L-01 'missing cap' framing and may warrant a severity re-evaluation of L-01 from Low to Medium. The finding proceeds to classification as still-open; finding-manager should update L-01's lastSeenRun to reflax-yield-vault-11 and append the new evidence note.
stillOpenMatches.recommendedLedgerAction: Update L-01 lastSeenRun=reflax-yield-vault-11; append MAX_BPS zero-principal and Halmos dust-loss evidence to L-01's notes; flag for severity re-evaluation (Low -> Medium boundary).

findings.title: emergencyWithdraw transfers vault shares to owner without updating clientBalances or totalDeposited, permanently corrupting the accounting ledger and making the strategy insolvent

medusaFailure.counterexample: depositForClient(seed, amount) then emergencyWithdrawPartial(amount): heldValue=285969984088074546357438, totalDeposited=416102355444464034513528, deficit=130132371356389488156090 wei

halmosFailure.counterexample: totalDeposited=0x8000000000000000, emergencySharesRemoved=0x800000000000000; totalValueAfter < totalDeposited, solvency invariant violated

forgeDirect.result: PASS — after 1000e18 deposit and full emergencyWithdraw, strategy holds 0 shares, principalOf returns 1000e18, heldValue (0) < totalDeposited (1000e18)

findings.rootCause: _emergencyWithdraw calls IERC20(address(vault)).safeTransfer(owner(), sharesToTransfer) without touching clientBalances[token][*] or totalDeposited[token]. The physical backing is removed but the principal ledger retains its pre-withdrawal values, making the strategy provably insolvent.
findings.impact: After emergencyWithdraw: (1) every subsequent client withdrawal receives less underlying than their credited principal; (2) _accrueSurplusShares finds totalValue < totalDeposited for all clients and returns zero surplus — yield collection is permanently bricked; (3) _totalWithdraw proportional calculations use stale totalDeposited as denominator, assigning inflated share fractions to remaining clients who then receive nothing because the shares are already gone.

findings.title: _totalWithdraw ignores the Phase-1 cached amount and re-reads live clientBalances, allowing inter-phase deposits to be silently extracted and causing underflow that bricks the two-phase withdrawal mechanism

tier3Evidence.halmos_SYMBOLIC_002: cachedAmount=0x800000000000, liveBalance=0xc00000000000 (+50%): sharesToSellBuggy uses liveBalance not cachedAmount; inter-phase deposit delta extracted as yield, depositor receives nothing
tier3Evidence.halmos_SYMBOLIC_004: cachedAmount=0x800000000000000000000000, liveBalance=0xc00000000000000000000000 (50% larger): actualDecrement=liveBalance, correctDecrement=cachedAmount; over-decrement by delta
tier3Evidence.halmos_SYMBOLIC_005: cachedAmount=interPhaseDeposit=otherClientBalance=0x800000000000: buggyRemainder=0 (double-counted), correctRemainder=2*otherClientBalance; inter-phase deposit principal vanishes
tier3Evidence.halmos_SYMBOLIC_006: liveBalance=2*cachedAmount > totalDepositedStale=cachedAmount: totalDeposited -= clientStoredBalance reverts with Solidity 0.8 checked arithmetic, permanently bricking Phase 2
tier3Evidence.forgeDirect: PASS — 1000e18 deposit, Phase 1 caches 1000, depositAsOwner(5000) interleaved, Phase 2 uses live balance 6000, owner receives 6000e18 not announced 1000e18

findings.rootCause: _totalWithdraw silently ignores its `amount` parameter (the Phase-1 cached balance) and re-reads clientStoredBalance = clientBalances[token][client] from live storage. Any principal added to the client between Phase 1 initiation and Phase 2 execution is included in the proportional share calculation and extracted by the owner without being covered by the 24-hour observation window. Additionally, if the live balance exceeds the stale totalDeposited, the subtraction totalDeposited -= clientStoredBalance reverts, permanently bricking the withdrawal path.
findings.impact: Three distinct impact paths proved by Halmos: (1) silent extraction of inter-phase deposits beyond the announced amount (rug amplification via depositAsOwner); (2) double-counting causing depositors to lose principal with no recovery path; (3) underflow revert that permanently locks the client's funds when the live balance exceeds the stale denominator. The 24-hour anti-rugpull notice mechanism is rendered ineffective for all cases.

findings.title: withdrawAsOwner completely bypasses the totalWithdrawal 24-hour timelock, making the anti-rugpull mechanism cosmetically ineffective — owner can atomically drain all client principal in a single block
findings.rootCause: withdrawAsOwner routes through _withdrawInternal with no timelock, no whenNotPaused check, and no pre-announcement requirement, while totalWithdrawal in AYieldStrategy implements a 24-hour two-phase waiting period explicitly to provide community protection against rugpulls. Both functions are accessible by the same onlyOwner key. The timelock mechanism is therefore circumventable at will.
findings.impact: A rogue or compromised owner calls withdrawAsOwner(client, attackerEOA, type(uint256).max) once per client in the same block. All client principal is converted and sent to an arbitrary recipient address with no 24-hour notice, no pause-gate, and no event field that identifies the debited client. The WithdrawalExecuted event that communities monitor to detect rugpulls is never emitted because the two-phase path is not taken.

findings.title: slippageToleranceBps defaults to 0 at deployment and accepts MAX_BPS (10000) as a valid setting — zero default over-credits depositor principal while MAX_BPS silently discards all principal credits
findings.newEvidenceVsL01: MAX_BPS path silently zeroes ALL depositor credited principal; Halmos formally proves dust-loss at any non-trivial slippage. Warrants severity re-evaluation of L-01 from Low toward Medium.

halmos_SYMBOLIC_001.counterexample: amount=4 wei, slippageBps=8192 (81.92%): 4*(10000-8192)/10000 = 7232/10000 = 0; depositor loses 4 wei with zero principal credited
halmos_SYMBOLIC_001.note: Also trivially: at MAX_BPS, amount*0/10000=0 for ALL amount.

findings.title: CEI violation in _withdrawInternal: state updates occur after two external calls, creating a latent reentrancy exposure that relies entirely on nonReentrant being preserved on all callers
findings.rootCause: Interactions-before-Effects ordering in _withdrawInternal: (1) ammAdapter.swap() external call at line 364, (2) underlyingToken.safeTransfer() to recipient at line 367, then (3) clientBalances decrement at line 371, (4) totalDeposited decrement at line 372. The nonReentrant modifier on all current public callers prevents immediate exploitation. Latent risk escalates if a new call path is added without nonReentrant, or if vault/underlying token implements ERC777 hooks.
findings.impact: Currently non-exploitable due to nonReentrant guards on all public entry points. Latent risk: double-withdrawal under any future refactoring or ERC777 token substitution.

findings.title: vault.convertToAssets / convertToShares used as price oracle across deposits, withdrawals, and surplus calculations — ERC4626 internal rate is manipulable by donating underlying to the vault, enabling DoS or over-extraction of surplus
findings.rootCause: All four economically sensitive computations trust vault.convertToAssets/convertToShares as an accurate price oracle. For vaults whose exchange rate is determined by totalAssets/totalSupply, a same-block donation of underlying inflates convertToAssets. This also inflates the surplus ceiling check (require totalShares <= convertToShares(aggregateSurplus)).
findings.impact: Primary realistic risk: DoS of deposit, withdrawal, and skimSurplus operations during a manipulated price spike (minOut becomes unsatisfiable, swap reverts). Secondary risk for skimSurplus: extraction of more underlying than the real yield warrants if the Curve pool tracks the vault's inflated rate. ECON-004 adds: the deposit solvency invariant is share-terms not underlying-terms, leaving a gap at AMM discount.

findings.title: safeIncreaseAllowance used unconditionally before every AMM swap without resetting to zero after completion — residual approvals accumulate under partial-revert conditions
findings.rootCause: safeIncreaseAllowance is additive. Under normal execution the residual is zero. However, if a swap reverts after approval is granted but before safeTransferFrom executes within the adapter, the residual persists across calls. Subsequent calls further accumulate it.
findings.impact: Under the current CurveAMMAdapter (atomic revert semantics), exploitability is near-zero. Under a future IAMMAdapter substitution where partial consumption is possible, accumulated allowances could allow the adapter to pull more than the strategy currently intends.

findings.title: abi.encodePacked() with dynamic-type arguments passed to keccak256 — potential hash collision
findings.rootCause: abi.encodePacked() with dynamic-length arguments produces ambiguous concatenations when passed to a hash function. Two distinct inputs can produce the same hash.
findings.impact: Severity depends on usage context. If the keccak256 result gates access control, validates state transitions, or identifies unique entities, collisions could allow spoofed authorization or duplicate-key attacks. Marked potential-medium pending manual confirmation of usage context.
findings.reviewNote: Manual review of AYieldStrategy.sol line 340 is needed to confirm how the keccak256 result is used before severity finalisation.

findings.title: CurveAMMAdapter.setRoute does not validate lastToken — uninitialized local variable accepted as route terminal token
findings.rootCause: The local variable `lastToken` in setRoute is declared but never initialized before being read as the route's terminal token validation anchor. An uninitialized local in Solidity defaults to address(0). This could allow a route to be registered with a zero terminal address that bypasses input-output token matching checks.
findings.impact: If route validation relies on lastToken matching the expected output token, address(0) would silently pass any check that compares lastToken to address(0), or silently fail any non-zero check. Either case allows misconfigured routes to be committed on-chain. A misconfigured route could direct swaps to an incorrect pool or token pair.
findings.noteVsL07: DEDUP-009 is a distinct sub-issue from L-07 (setRoute accepts tokenIn==tokenOut). L-07 covers missing equality check and zero-gap segments; DEDUP-009 covers the uninitialized lastToken local variable. Both are in setRoute but have different root causes and different remediations.

findings.title: emergencyWithdraw lacks nonReentrant guard — inconsistent with all other state-changing entry points; latent risk if vault token implements transfer callbacks
findings.rootCause: AYieldStrategy.emergencyWithdraw is decorated with onlyOwner but not nonReentrant. Every other state-changing external entry point uses nonReentrant. The asymmetry creates a gap: if the vault token implements ERC777 tokensReceived hooks, the owner's receiver contract gets control mid-transfer with the reentrancy mutex NOT held.
findings.impact: Low probability for the intended sUSDe vault deployment (standard ERC20). Escalates to concrete risk for any future vault integration with transfer hooks.

findings.title: nonReentrant is not the first modifier in function declaration lists across multiple entry points — modifiers before nonReentrant can execute with reentrancy mutex not yet locked
findings.function: multiple (lines 319, 366 in AYieldStrategy.sol; lines 229, 248, 265, 279 in ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol)
findings.rootCause: Solidity applies modifiers in declaration order. Earlier modifiers (onlyOwner, whenNotPaused, onlyAuthorizedClient) execute before the reentrancy lock is acquired. A malicious modifier body or a modifier with an external call could reenter the contract before the mutex is set.
findings.impact: Low severity in practice: the earlier modifiers do not make external calls. Purely structural risk for future modifier additions.

findings.title: Constructor _owner shadowing across three contracts — local parameter hides inherited Ownable._owner state variable
findings.rootCause: All three constructors declare a local parameter named `_owner` which shadows the inherited Ownable._owner state variable. Benign here because the constructors immediately pass `_owner` to the Ownable initializer. If any future constructor logic reads `_owner` expecting the state variable, it would silently read the parameter.
findings.impact: No current security impact. Code quality finding to prevent future confusion.

findings.title: WithdrawalExecuted event emits the Phase-1 cached balance rather than the actual amount transferred — produces misleading on-chain records that compound the CODE-001 discrepancy
findings.rootCause: WithdrawalExecuted emits withdrawAmount = state.balance (Phase-1 cached snapshot). ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy._totalWithdraw ignores this value and operates on the live clientStoredBalance. When clientBalances grew between phases, the event records a smaller amount than actually transferred.
findings.impact: Off-chain monitoring systems receive incorrect withdrawal amounts. The misleading event compresses the observability of the DEDUP-002 bug — community members watching for rugpull signals cannot detect inter-phase enlargement from the WithdrawalExecuted event alone.

findings.title: withdrawAsOwner debits client's principal while allowing tokens to be sent to an arbitrary recipient — no event field identifies which client was drained
findings.rootCause: withdrawAsOwner(client, recipient, amount) debits clientBalances[token][client] but routes underlying to recipient. The emitted Withdrawn event records msg.sender (owner) and recipient but omits client as an indexed field. Automated monitoring cannot determine which client's balance was debited without additional storage reads.
findings.impact: In a multi-client deployment, a forced extraction from one client leaves that client's internal accounting inconsistent with the strategy's ledger, with no on-chain signal linking the Withdrawn event to the debited client address.

findings.title: Ownable used instead of Ownable2Step across all three contracts — ownership transfer is irreversible if the new owner address is incorrect
findings.rootCause: Both contracts use OpenZeppelin Ownable rather than Ownable2Step. A single-step ownership transfer is irreversible if the new owner address is a typo, a contract without the expected interface, or a compromised address.
findings.impact: Low severity operational risk; not an active exploit path. Remediable by migrating to Ownable2Step.

findings.title: ERC4626 vault used as price oracle in surplus and skimSurplus calculations — two consecutive convertToAssets calls in the same transaction may return different rates for time-weighted vaults, causing revert
findings.rootCause: Inside _skimSurplus, vault.convertToAssets is called at the top to snapshot totalValue, and again at the bottom to compute minOut from totalShares. For vaults with accrual-triggered rates, these two calls can return different rates within the same transaction. If the second call returns a higher rate, minOut becomes unsatisfiable and the swap reverts.
findings.impact: Temporary DoS on skimSurplus — no fund loss, retry resolves it. Narrow sub-case of DEDUP-006's broader vault oracle risk.

findings.title: totalBalanceOf and principalOf use different data sources — live vault price vs. static accounting value — creating inconsistent paired views that can return negative yield for downstream integrators
findings.rootCause: totalBalanceOf returns a vault-price-sensitive value while principalOf returns a static clientBalances value. After a vault price decline, totalBalanceOf < principalOf. Any integrating contract computing totalBalanceOf - principalOf as a yield signal receives a negative value, potentially reverting on unchecked underflow or triggering incorrect downstream logic.
findings.impact: Low severity in isolation; elevated risk for downstream protocols that assume totalBalanceOf >= principalOf as an invariant. No fund loss in the strategy itself.

findings.title: CurveAMMAdapter.swap does not independently verify amountOut >= minAmountOut after router returns — delegates floor enforcement entirely to Curve Router NG
findings.rootCause: After router.exchange returns amountOut, no require(amountOut >= minAmountOut) check is performed. The strategy trusts the Curve Router NG's internal _min_dy enforcement exclusively. A misconfigured, buggy, or future-upgraded router could return a below-floor value without the adapter detecting it.
findings.impact: Low in practice: the router is immutable and battle-tested. Risk only materialises under a future strategy redeployment with an incorrect router address. Defense-in-depth recommendation.

suppressionLog.reason: Exact semantic match to L-02 (wont-fix). DEDUP-013 (unbounded client loop OOG) and L-02 (skimSurplus unbounded iteration, no pagination) describe the same root cause. L-02 was triaged wont-fix with author acknowledgement that the client count will remain bounded. story-042's _distributeBuffer addition doubles the per-iteration constant but was already noted in L-02's reconfirmation at run-07. No new attack surface justifying reopening.

The deduplicator's own rootCause text states the NatSpec 'explicitly acknowledges this as a known acceptable tradeoff for the current all-protocol-owned-client model'. The buffer front-run sub-case (ECON-010) is likewise noted as acknowledged in NatSpec. Design decisions documented in NatSpec are treated equivalently to known issues under the sanitizer's mandate. The reflax-yield-vault designDecisions entry ('Principal is decremented by REQUESTED amount on withdraw, not RECEIVED amount — any shortfall accrues to protocol') establishes the same philosophy. This finding contributes no new security surface above what is explicitly accepted by the protocol.
